subject: Urgent: Elevated 5xx/429 + streaming timeouts — MedSync
messages:
From: Robert Li <robert.li@medsync.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.ai>
Cc: eng-ops@medsync.com
Date: Wed, 11 Apr 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Production issues — spikes in 5xx/429 and streaming disconnects

Sean —

We started seeing a spike in 5xx/429 responses to our streaming chat endpoints around 08:45 PT. Users are getting disconnected mid-conversation; some clients are retrying aggressively and creating a retry spiral. Attaching a Grafana snapshot.

Key impact: multiple live sessions dropped during peak (08:45–09:05), elevated 5xx rate ~4.2% (baseline ~0.1%), a noticeable uptick in client-side timeouts at 10s. Our on-call saw CPU and queue depth climb on the dedicated pool.

We need immediate guidance on mitigation and a short-term workaround while you investigate. Can you advise timeout/backoff recommendations and whether we should route to a fallback model?

—Robert
Head of Platform, MedSync Health
(attachment: medsync_grafana_5xx_spike.png)
From: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.ai>
To: Robert Li <robert.li@medsync.com>
Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 11 Apr 2028 09:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Production issues — spikes in 5xx/429 and streaming disconnects

Robert — thanks for the heads up and the Grafana shot. We're triaging now. Quick asks while we investigate:

- Can you confirm the client retry policy (initial backoff, max attempts)?
- Are the timeouts happening at ~10s consistently or variable?
- Any correlation with a model change or traffic shift (A/B test)?

Immediate mitigations we recommend:
- Increase client idle/read timeout to 30s while we look for idle disconnect causes.
- If you have client-side exponential backoff, cap retries to 3 attempts and jitter.
- We'll try a temporary routing policy to a compatible model variant with lower memory pressure if capacity is causing 5xx.

Vanessa/Evelyn — looping you in to lead the operational response and coordinate an exec update if needed. I'll stand by for any further data.

Sean
Enterprise AE, Redwood Inference
Redwood Inference — Developer-first LLM inference

From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.ai>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 11 Apr 2028 09:27:00 -07:00
Subject: Fwd: Production issues — spikes in 5xx/429 and streaming disconnects

Sean — forwarding for ops plan. Summary: MedSync active sessions dropped, 5xx/429 spike, client-side timeouts at ~10s, retry amplification observed.

Action plan (initial):
1) Contain:
   - Apply an immediate routing rule to send new sessions to a lower-concurrency dedicated pool in us-west-2 (compatible model variant: redwood-compat-medium).
   - Enable aggressive KV-cache sharing on the pool (TTL 30m) to reduce token compute.
2) Limit retries:
   - Push a recommended client policy to MedSync (cap retries to 3, backoff starting at 300ms with full jitter).
3) Observe:
   - Add short retention of detailed traces for the affected model route for 72h.
4) Exec comms:
   - If 5xx > 2% after 30m, prepare a one-pager for CTO, include impact and mitigation steps.

Attachments: streaming runbook excerpt and Grafana screenshot included in thread.

I'll take lead on routing and cache config; Evelyn, can you coordinate tracing and runbook ops?

—Vanessa
Sr. Reliability PM, Redwood Inference
(attachment: redwood_streaming_runbook_v2.pdf)
From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.ai>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>, Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.ai>
Cc: Robert Li <robert.li@medsync.com>
Date: Wed, 11 Apr 2028 10:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Production issues — spikes in 5xx/429 and streaming disconnects

Quick updates from runtime team:
- We applied the routing rule at 09:38 PT. New session throughput routed to redwood-compat-medium pool.
- Enabled KV-cache sharing; observed median per-token latency drop ~18% in the next 4m.
- Tracing enabled and collected; initial traces indicate a backlog at the tokenization stage for sessions with very long prefixes.

Recommended immediate customer-facing guidance (send to MedSync):
- Adjust client-side idle/read timeout to 30s and implement capped exponential backoff (max attempts = 3, base = 300ms, max backoff = 10s).
- For long-prefix use cases, consider prefix pruning on client before streaming.

Robert — we also pushed a temporary rate-smoothing rule to avoid sudden bursts from your web-socket proxies (smoothed by a 500ms token emission window). Please validate on your side.

Evelyn
Staff SRE, Redwood Inference
From: Robert Li <robert.li@medsync.com>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.ai>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>, Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 11 Apr 2028 10:34:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Production issues — spikes in 5xx/429 and streaming disconnects

Thanks — we applied the timeout/backoff changes and saw an immediate reduction in client-side retries. The Grafana window shows 5xx dropping from 4.2% to ~1.1% over 20 minutes. Some notes:

- The disconnected sessions were from our mobile clients that aggressively retry after 8–10s. The change to 30s and capped retries helped.
- We still see intermittent 429s during short burst windows when several dozen users start new sessions simultaneously. Those appear tied to our proxy fan-out pattern.

We'd like a short executive summary for our CTO and a runbook snippet we can embed in our incident playbook. Can you provide a one-page note and the runbook PDF you referenced?

—Robert
From: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.ai>
To: Robert Li <robert.li@medsync.com>
Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 12 Apr 2028 16:40:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Production issues — spikes in 5xx/429 and streaming disconnects

Robert — glad to hear the mitigation helped. Attaching a one-page exec summary and the relevant runbook excerpt; Vanessa also prepared a short note on routing and cache changes.

Next steps we recommend for MedSync:
- Keep the client timeout at 30s for now and monitor user impact for 48h.
- Work with your proxy/edge team to smooth connection fan-out (stagger new session requests by 200–500ms).
- If you plan heavy A/B or full-rollout traffic increases, coordinate a capacity bump with us for the dedicated pool.

I'll schedule a 30-minute postmortem with our teams for tomorrow to review traces and finalize a permanent mitigation.

Sean Gallagher
Enterprise AE, Redwood Inference
